audio.t: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Pinewood Adventure Camp. My name is Claire, and I will be your group leader this week.
First, a few words about the timetable. Breakfast is at eight, and the first activity starts at nine thirty. Please do not be late, because the minibus for the lake leaves at nine twenty-five.

On Monday and Tuesday you will learn to paddle a canoe. On Wednesday we will walk up Eagle Hill, and I suggest wearing strong shoes, because the path is rocky. Thursday is the day for the climbing wall.

You will sleep in tents, four people in each. Your teachers have already chosen the groups, but you can ask me if you want to change. Please keep your phones in your bags during the day. You can use them after dinner for one hour.

If you are hungry between meals, there is a small shop near the dining hall that sells fruit and sandwiches. And on Friday evening we will have a big campfire, where each team will perform a short song or a story.
Finally, remember that the weather in the hills changes quickly, so bring a warm jacket as well as a raincoat. Now, let's go and find your tents.

audio.t: Today my guest is Leo Park, who is seventeen and plays the drums in a school band called Blue Rocket. Leo, how did you start?
My uncle gave me an old drum kit when I was ten. At first I only made noise, but then I found videos online and learned the basic rhythms.
Did you take lessons?
Only for six months. My teacher was good, but I preferred to play with other people. That is why I joined the school band, and it was the best decision I made.
How often does the band practice?
Twice a week after school, on Tuesdays and Thursdays. It used to be three times, but we all have exams this year, so we reduced it.
What is the hardest part of being in a band?
Honestly, not the music. It is agreeing on what to play. Four people have four different tastes, and sometimes we argue for an hour about one song.
And you have a concert soon, I believe.
Yes, at the end of the month, in the school hall. We are a bit nervous, because it is the first time we will play our own songs and not songs by other bands.
What do you hope to do in the future?
I would like to study music at college, but I will probably do it as a hobby and choose a job in engineering, because it is safer. But I will never stop playing.

items.text:
When I was fourteen, my parents told me we were moving from our village to the city. I was shocked. I imagined noisy streets, crowded buses and no green space at all. We would live in a flat on the twelfth floor, and I had never lived above the ground. I cried that night, and for the first month I told everybody that I hated it.

Slowly, however, my opinion began to change. The first surprise was how easy everything was. In the village, the nearest cinema was an hour away by car, and the bus to school only came twice a day. Now I could walk to my school in ten minutes, and the library, the swimming pool and my favorite bakery were all in the same neighborhood. I stopped asking my parents for lifts and started to feel independent.

The second surprise was the people. I had expected city dwellers to be cold and unfriendly, but in our building an old woman called Mrs. Patel invited us for tea in the first week. Later I met a group of students who ran a small garden on the roof, and I joined them. We grew tomatoes and herbs between the chimneys, and I realized that nature does not disappear in cities; you just have to look for it in different places.

Of course, city life is not perfect. The traffic is loud, the air is not as fresh as in the countryside, and I still miss the silence of the village at night. Housing is also expensive, which is why our flat is so small that I share a room with my little brother. Sometimes we argue about the light.

Even so, I would not go back now. Moving taught me that change is frightening only until you give it a chance. If your family is planning a move, my advice is simple: do not decide in advance how you will feel.

items.q:
Read the email from your English friend Chris and write a reply of about 100 words.

Hi! Next month our class is going on a school trip to a farm for two days. We will sleep in a barn and help feed the animals. I am not sure what to pack. What do you think I should bring? Have you ever slept away from home? Do you want to hear about the trip when I get back?

Write about: what to pack, a time you slept away from home, and whether you would like to hear about the trip.
items.sample: Hi Chris, thanks for your email. The farm trip sounds like a fantastic adventure! I think you should bring warm clothes, because nights in a barn can be cold, and a pair of old boots for the mud. A flashlight and a water bottle are also very useful. I have slept away from home several times. Last summer I stayed with my cousins in the mountains for a week, and we told ghost stories every night. At first I missed my own bed, but then I got used to it. I would love to hear about your trip when you get back, especially about the animals. Please send me some photos too. Have a great time, and write soon! Best wishes, Minh
items.vi: Trả lời đủ ba ý: nên mang gì, lần ngủ xa nhà, và có muốn nghe về chuyến đi. Dùng lời chào và lời kết thân mật.

items.q: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story for the school magazine. Your story must begin with this sentence: The lights suddenly went out, and the whole street became dark. Write your story in about 100 words.
items.sample: The lights suddenly went out, and the whole street became dark. I was alone in the apartment, because my parents were working late. At first I felt afraid, but then I remembered the flashlight in the kitchen drawer. I walked carefully along the corridor and found it. When I opened the door, I saw my neighbors standing on the stairs with candles. An old man named Mr. Lopez smiled and said that the whole building had lost power. We all sat together and shared hot tea and cookies. Somebody started to sing, and soon everybody joined in. When the lights came back two hours later, I was almost sorry. It had been the best evening of the year.
items.vi: Bắt đầu đúng câu cho sẵn; kể theo thứ tự thời gian, dùng thì quá khứ và có phần kết.

audio.t: Hello and welcome to Green Fingers. Today I'm going to talk about growing vegetables on a small balcony. Many people believe that you need a big garden, but that is not true. All you need is a few pots, good soil and some sunshine.

The first thing to check is the sun. Most vegetables need at least five hours of light every day, so choose the sunniest corner. If your balcony is shady, don't worry. Lettuce and spinach grow well in shade.
For beginners, I suggest cherry tomatoes. Many people say tomatoes are difficult, but the small ones are quite easy. They only need water every morning in the summer.
Use pots with holes in the bottom, because too much water is the main reason why plants die. You can also save money by using old plastic bottles or tins as pots. I did that last spring.
And next week on the program, we will visit a school garden where children grow herbs for the school kitchen. Join us then.

audio.t: Today I'm talking to Dr. Hana Ortiz, who studies sleep. Dr. Ortiz, how much sleep do teenagers need?
Most need between eight and ten hours a night, but many get only six or seven.
Why is that?
Partly because the body clock changes in the teenage years, so they feel sleepy later at night. But phones play a part too. The light from a screen tells the brain that it is still daytime.
Should schools start later?
Some schools that started one hour later saw good results. Students were less tired in lessons. However, it is hard for families to change their timetables.
What advice do you give?
Stop using screens an hour before bed. Reading a book is better. Also, avoid drinks with caffeine after lunch. A lot of students are surprised by that.
What about sleeping late at the weekend?
A small lie-in is fine, but more than two hours makes Monday harder.
Do you have a final tip?
Keep your room cool and dark. Temperature matters more than people think.

items.text:
Three ways to help in our town

Paws Haven
Paws Haven is an animal shelter on Mill Road. Volunteers walk the dogs and clean the cages on Saturday mornings from 8 to 12. No experience is needed, but please wear old clothes. Volunteers must be 13 or older, and anyone under 16 needs a parent's signature.

Reading Buddies
Every Tuesday and Thursday from 4 to 5 p.m., volunteers read with children aged six to eight at Oakfield Primary School. Volunteers must be at least 14 and must come to a training session on the first Tuesday of the month.

Riverside Clean-Up
On the second Sunday of every month, a big group meets at the old bridge from 9 to 12 to collect garbage along the river. Gloves and bags are provided, and there is a free lunch for everyone afterward. The minimum age is 12.

items.text:
When my teacher first suggested that I should spend Wednesday afternoons at Willow Court Care Home, I was not excited. I was fourteen, I had a lot of homework, and I honestly thought that old people would find a teenager boring. I only agreed because the school offered a certificate to volunteers, which I thought would look good on my future applications.

My first visit was a disaster. I had planned to read aloud from a funny adventure book, but the residents were not interested at all, and one man fell asleep after five minutes. I felt embarrassed and nearly gave up. On the way out, though, a woman called Mrs. Alvarez asked me if I could help her write a letter to her grandson, because she could not see well enough to write. That small request changed everything.

Over the next weeks, I discovered that the residents did not want entertainment; they wanted company. Mrs. Alvarez told me stories about growing up on a farm with no electricity, and Mr. Kwan taught me to play chess, although he beat me nineteen times in a row. I started to look forward to Wednesdays more than any other day.

Of course, volunteering is not always easy. Sometimes I arrive tired after a long day at school, and there are afternoons when a resident is sad or unwell, which is hard to see. My mother says that these feelings show that I really care. I think she is right.

The certificate arrived last month and, strangely, I almost forgot to collect it. What I value more now is the confidence I have gained. I used to be shy with adults, but now I can talk to almost anybody. I have also learned to listen, which is more difficult than it sounds.

Next year I would like to start a reading club at the home with some of my classmates. A few have said that they are nervous, so I tell them what Mrs. Alvarez once told me: "Nobody is boring if you ask the right questions." I think this is the best advice I have ever received.

options: Her teacher made her do it.
She thought a certificate would help her later.
She wanted to meet old people.

items.q:
You received this email from your English friend Alex.

Hi! I want to start a new sport this year, but I can't decide which one. Which sport would you recommend? Where can I practice it? Do I need to buy any special equipment?

Write an email to Alex. Say which sport you recommend and why, tell Alex where to practice, and explain what equipment is needed.
items.sample: Hi Alex, thanks for your email. I am happy that you want to start a new sport. I recommend badminton because it is fun, cheap and easy to learn. You do not need to be very strong or fast, and you can play with friends or family. You can practice at the sports hall near the library. It is open every evening, and it only costs two dollars for an hour. If you prefer to play outside, the park has a free court, but you need good weather. About equipment, you only need a racket, some shuttlecocks and comfortable shoes. I can lend you my old racket until you decide to buy your own. If you like, we can play together on Saturday morning. I think you will really enjoy it. Write back soon and tell me what you decide. Best wishes, Linh

I could not see anything, so I took out my phone and turned on the flashlight. Suddenly, I heard a strange sound from the kitchen. My heart was beating fast, but I walked slowly toward it. When I opened the kitchen door, I saw my grandmother standing there with a candle and a big smile. She said that she had been waiting for me. The strange sound was only her old radio, which works with batteries. We sat together at the table, ate the soup by candlelight and told funny stories. Finally, the lights came back on after an hour. I was a little sad because the evening in the dark was so special.

audio.t: Today I am talking to Leo Marsh, a fifteen-year-old climber who has just won a national youth title. Leo, how did you start?
By accident, really. My cousin took me to an indoor climbing wall for his birthday when I was nine. I thought I would hate it, because I was afraid of heights, but I could not wait to go back.
How often do you train now?
Five days a week, usually for two hours after school. On Sundays I rest completely. My coach says rest is as important as training, and I have learned that he is right.
Is climbing a dangerous sport?
People think so, but indoors it is quite safe if you follow the rules. The hardest part is not the fear, it is staying calm when your arms are tired and the next hold is far away.
What do you eat before a competition?
Something simple, like rice and a banana. In the past I tried a big breakfast and felt heavy on the wall, so I never do that now.
What are your plans for the future?

Next year I want to enter the international junior contest. But I also want to study engineering, so school comes first. Climbing is a hobby that I love, and I do not want to lose that feeling by making it too serious.
Good luck, Leo, and thank you.

items.text:
Three Creative Workshops This Summer

Clay Corner: Learn to make bowls, cups and small animals with your hands. No experience is needed and all the materials are included. Pixel Lab: Make your own short animations on a computer. You will draw characters, add sound and show your film to families on the last day. You must bring your own headphones. The workshop runs every morning for five days and is for students who are already comfortable using computers. Ages 12 to 17.

Sketch Walk: Every Saturday afternoon the group walks around the old town with a teacher and draws buildings, bridges and people. Bring a pencil and a notebook, or buy them at the first meeting for a small fee. It is the cheapest of the three workshops, and there is no age limit. items.text:
Through Her Lens

When Mira Solano was twelve, she borrowed her uncle's old camera to take pictures of her cat. The photos were blurry and dark, but she remembers feeling that she had discovered a secret language. Today, at sixteen, she runs a small online gallery of pictures from the busy market in her home town, and her work has been shown in the town hall.

Mira says that the market was not an obvious choice. 'Everyone told me to photograph the beach or the mountains,' she explains. 'But I was always at the market with my grandmother, and I noticed that the stalls changed with every season. The colors of the fruit, the hands of the sellers, the steam from the food stands, all of it told a story.'

She now goes every Sunday at six in the morning, when the light is soft and the crowds are small. At first, people were suspicious. A few sellers refused to be photographed, which she understood. 'I learned to talk first and take pictures later,' she says. 'Now many of them ask me when I am coming back.' One fish seller even keeps a chair for her.

Technical skills did not come quickly. Mira spent a year learning how to hold the camera still and how to use natural light. She watched videos, read library books and asked local photographers for advice. Some of them were generous. Others, she says with a laugh, 'told me to try painting instead.' She did not give up.

Her proudest moment came last winter, when an elderly customer saw a photograph of her late husband selling oranges thirty years ago. Mira had found the picture in the market's old archive and printed it for the exhibition. The woman cried and asked for a copy. 'That day I understood why I take photographs,' Mira says. 'It is not about perfect pictures. It is about keeping people and places from disappearing.'

Mira hopes to study photography at university, but she is worried that she may lose her style if she is taught too many rules. For now, she plans to carry on at the market, and she has promised her grandmother a book of the best pictures.

She was disappointed by her blurry photos.
She wanted to become a famous artist.

items.text:
Three ways to explore space this summer

A. Starlight Camp
This five-day camp in the hills of Dunmore is for students aged 13 to 16. Campers sleep in tents and spend every night looking at planets and stars through large telescopes. Experts teach them to read star maps, and on the last evening everyone builds a small model rocket and launches it. No experience is needed, but campers must bring their own sleeping bag. The camp costs $180, including meals.

B. Orion Science Lab
Orion Science Lab, in the center of Marlow, is open every day of the year. Visitors can touch a real piece of rock from Mars, try on a space suit, and watch a film about astronauts on the Space Station. Every Saturday morning, there is a workshop where teenagers design robots that could explore other planets. Tickets are $12, and children under 12 must come with an adult.

C. Moonwatch Club
The Moonwatch Club meets in the school hall every Thursday evening at 6:30, and it is free to join. Members share photos of the night sky, listen to talks from local scientists, and take turns to use the club's telescope in the park. Members do not stay overnight, but once a month the club organizes a trip to see the sky away from the city lights. Newcomers are always welcome, and many members are adults.

items.text:
Last winter, my uncle Ray gave me his old telescope. It was twenty years old, heavy and covered in dust, and honestly, I was a little disappointed. I had hoped for a new phone. I put the box under my bed and forgot about it for two months.

Then, in February, our science teacher, Mr. Ellison, told us that Saturn would be easy to see that month. I decided to give the telescope a try. It took me an hour to put it together because half the instructions were missing, and my little sister laughed at me when I dropped one of the lenses on the carpet. Luckily, nothing broke.

That night, the sky was perfectly clear. My father drove me to a field outside town, where there were no street lights. At first, I could see nothing but a blur. Then I turned a small wheel, and suddenly there it was: a tiny golden planet with a ring around it. I actually laughed out loud. I had seen hundreds of pictures of Saturn in books, but nothing prepared me for seeing it with my own eyes. Knowing that the light had traveled for more than an hour to reach me made me feel very small, but in a good way.

Some of my friends say that watching the sky is pointless when you can look at much sharper photographs on the internet. I understand what they mean, and I do use those photographs when I study. But I disagree. A picture is something that somebody else has made for you. When you find a planet yourself, after waiting in the cold for forty minutes, it belongs to you in a special way.

Since that night, I have joined the school astronomy club, and I have learned that you do not need expensive equipment to start. Our club leader says that a pair of ordinary binoculars is enough to see the moons of Jupiter. What you really need is patience, a warm coat and a dark place. I am now saving up to buy a better lens for Uncle Ray's telescope. I will never again judge a present by its box.

items.q: How did the writer feel when he first received the telescope?
items.vi: Ông bác tặng kính thiên văn cũ, cậu hơi thất vọng vì mong có một chiếc điện thoại mới.

items.q: What went wrong when he put the telescope together?
options: His sister took a part away.
Some of the instructions were missing.
He broke one of the lenses.
items.vi: Một nửa hướng dẫn bị mất nên cậu mất cả giờ mới lắp xong; thấu kính chỉ bị rơi chứ không vỡ.

items.q: How did he feel when he saw Saturn?
options: Afraid of how far away it was
Sad because it looked so small
items.vi: Cậu bật cười thành tiếng và cảm thấy mình nhỏ bé nhưng theo nghĩa tích cực.

items.q: What does he think about his friends' opinion on watching the sky?
options: He agrees that it is pointless.
He thinks photographs are no use for study.
Finding a planet yourself is more special.
items.vi: Cậu hiểu bạn mình nhưng không đồng ý: tự tìm ra một hành tinh mang lại cảm giác đặc biệt hơn xem ảnh.

items.q: What is the writer's main purpose in the text?
options: To explain how to build a telescope
To persuade readers to buy a new telescope
To describe how a gift changed his attitude
items.vi: Bài viết kể món quà cũ ban đầu bị chê đã thay đổi cách nghĩ của cậu như thế nào.

parts.instr: Five sentences have been removed from the paragraphs. Choose the correct sentence for each gap.
parts.instrVi: Mỗi đoạn văn thiếu một câu. Chọn câu đúng cho mỗi chỗ trống.

items.text: Many people think astronauts spend all day floating happily. ＿ They have to exercise for two hours every day to keep their muscles and bones strong. Without exercise, their bodies would become weak in space.
items.q: Choose the best sentence for the gap.
options: Some astronauts return to Earth after six months.
The Station travels around the Earth very fast.
Astronauts eat their meals from special packets.
In fact, life on the Space Station is hard work.
items.vi: Câu sau nói họ phải tập thể dục hai giờ mỗi ngày, nên câu thiếu phải nói cuộc sống trên trạm là công việc vất vả.

items.text: Our Moon has no air and no wind. ＿ This is why the footprints left by astronauts long ago are still there today. They may stay for millions of years.
items.q: Choose the best sentence for the gap.
options: Many people enjoy looking at it.
It is much colder than Earth at night.
The Moon is about 384,000 kilometers from Earth.
Nothing moves the dust on its surface.
items.vi: Vì không có không khí hay gió nên không gì làm xê dịch lớp bụi, do đó dấu chân vẫn còn nguyên.

items.text: Last week our class visited the observatory. We were told to wear warm clothes, because the building is not heated. ＿ Nobody wanted to leave when the visit finished.
items.q: Choose the best sentence for the gap.
options: The bus left the school at nine o'clock.
It was my first time at the cinema.
Our teacher forgot to bring her camera.
Inside, the guide showed us the giant telescope and let us look through it.
items.vi: Câu sau nói không ai muốn ra về, nên câu thiếu kể về điều thú vị bên trong đài quan sát.

items.text: Scientists have found thousands of planets that go around other stars. ＿ For life as we know it, a planet must be neither too hot nor too cold, so that water can stay liquid. Only a few of these worlds seem to be like that.
items.q: Choose the best sentence for the gap.
options: Most of them were discovered by a team of students.
Telescopes have become cheaper every year.
These stars are much brighter than our Sun.
However, finding one where people could live is much harder.
items.vi: Câu sau giải thích điều kiện để có sự sống, nên câu thiếu nói rằng tìm hành tinh phù hợp khó hơn nhiều.

items.text: On the first day of the space camp, we learned how rockets work. ＿ We used plastic bottles, water and a bicycle pump, and the winning bottle flew almost twenty meters high. Everyone cheered.
items.q: Choose the best sentence for the gap.
options: Next summer I would like to go there again.
My brother wants to be an astronaut one day.
The camp is in the mountains, far from big cities.
After lunch, we built our own simple rockets and had a competition.
items.vi: Câu sau nhắc đến chai nhựa, nước và bơm xe đạp, tức là cách làm tên lửa trong cuộc thi.

parts.instr: For each question, choose the correct word for the gap.
parts.instrVi: Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn từ đúng cho chỗ trống.

items.text: She knows a great ＿ about planets, and she can name every one of them in the right order.
items.q: Choose the correct word.

items.text: The rocket launch was delayed ＿ of bad weather.
items.q: Choose the correct word.
items.vi: Cấu trúc đúng là because of bad weather (vì thời tiết xấu).

items.text: The new telescope will allow scientists to ＿ distant galaxies in more detail than ever before.
items.q: Choose the correct word.
items.vi: Examine nghĩa là xem xét kỹ, hợp với việc nghiên cứu các thiên hà xa xôi.

items.text: It is ＿ that the first people on Mars will be adults, not children.
items.q: Choose the correct word.
items.vi: Cấu trúc It is likely that... (có khả năng là); probably, perhaps, maybe không đứng sau It is.

items.text: He was so ＿ in his book about stars that he did not hear me come in.
items.q: Choose the correct word.
items.vi: Cụm đúng là be interested in (quan tâm, hứng thú với).

items.text: Please ＿ me know if you cannot come to the astronomy club on Friday.
items.q: Choose the correct word.
items.vi: Cụm let me know nghĩa là cho tôi biết.

parts.instr: Write ONE word for each gap.
parts.instrVi: Viết MỘT từ cho mỗi chỗ trống.

items.text: The Earth takes one year to go ＿ the Sun.
items.vi: Go around the Sun nghĩa là quay quanh Mặt Trời.

items.text: If it ＿ cloudy tonight, we won't see any stars.
items.vi: Câu điều kiện loại 1: If + hiện tại đơn, nên dùng is.

items.text: Jupiter is much bigger ＿ the Earth.
items.vi: So sánh hơn dùng bigger than.

items.vi: Dùng since với mốc thời gian trong quá khứ và thì hiện tại hoàn thành.

items.vi: Câu hỏi gián tiếp dạng Yes/No dùng whether hoặc if.

items.text: The telescope, ＿ was built in 1950, still works perfectly.
items.vi: Mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định có dấu phẩy dùng which.

parts.instr: Write an email reply.
parts.instrVi: Viết thư trả lời.

items.q:
Read the email from your English friend Ruby. Write a reply of at least 100 words.
Hi! My parents say I can learn a musical instrument this year, but I can't decide which one. I like the guitar, but the piano looks easier. What do you think? Do you play an instrument? Also, would you like to start a band with me this summer?
Ruby
In your reply: say which instrument you think is better and why; tell Ruby about your own experience of music; answer her question about the band.
items.sample: Hi Ruby, Thanks for your email. It is great news that your parents will let you learn an instrument! I think the guitar is a better choice than the piano, because you can carry it anywhere and play it with friends at the park or on the beach. The piano is easier at the beginning, but it is very big and you can only play it at home. I played the flute for two years at primary school, but I stopped because my teacher moved away. Now I just listen to music on the bus every day, and I sometimes sing in the school choir. I would love to start a band with you this summer! I can sing and I could learn a little drum rhythm. We could practice every Saturday afternoon in my garage. Please write back soon and tell me what you decide. Best wishes, Lan
items.vi: Trả lời đủ ba ý: chọn nhạc cụ và nêu lý do, kể kinh nghiệm âm nhạc của bạn, và trả lời lời mời lập ban nhạc. Dùng because, but, and để nối câu.

parts.instr: Write a story.
parts.instrVi: Viết một câu chuyện.

items.q: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story for the school magazine. Your story must begin with this sentence: It was the best surprise of my life. Write your story in at least 100 words.
items.sample: It was the best surprise of my life. I had just come home from school on my birthday, feeling a little sad because nobody had said anything about it all day. I opened the front door and the house was completely dark. Suddenly, the lights came on and thirty people shouted, Happy birthday! My cousins, my classmates and even my old neighbors were all standing in the living room. My mother had been planning the party for weeks, and everyone had kept the secret. There was a big chocolate cake on the table, and my brother had made a long banner with my name on it. I was so happy that I could not speak for a minute. Finally, I laughed and hugged my mother. We danced and played games until it was very late, and I will never forget that evening.
items.vi: Mở đầu bằng câu đề bài cho sẵn, kể theo thứ tự thời gian, dùng các từ nối như suddenly, finally và thì quá khứ đơn.

parts.instr: Answer the questions about yourself.
parts.instrVi: Trả lời các câu hỏi về bản thân.

items.q: What do you usually do in the evening after you finish your homework?
items.sample: In the evening I usually watch a funny video with my family, and then I read a book before I go to bed.
items.vi: Nói về thói quen buổi tối: dùng usually và các hoạt động hằng ngày.

items.q: Tell me about a meal that you like cooking or eating with your family.
items.sample: My favorite family meal is fish soup with rice, because my grandmother cooks it on Sundays and we all eat together.
items.vi: Nêu một bữa ăn yêu thích và giải thích lý do bằng because.

items.q: How often do you play sports or do exercise, and which do you enjoy most?
items.sample: I often do exercise, about three times a week, and I enjoy badminton most because it is fast and I play with my friends.
items.vi: Nói về tần suất tập thể thao (often, times a week) và môn yêu thích.

items.q: Do you prefer hot weather or cold weather? Why?
items.sample: I prefer cool weather, because in hot weather I feel tired and I cannot play outside in the afternoon.
items.vi: Dùng prefer ... because để nêu sở thích và lý do.

parts.instr: Describe the photo.
parts.instrVi: Mô tả bức ảnh.

items.q: Look at the photo. Describe what the people are doing and say how you think they feel.
items.sample: In this photo, I can see a family in a kitchen. They are cooking a pizza together. The father is putting cheese on the pizza, and a girl is holding a bowl. I think they are very happy because they are smiling and working as a team. Maybe it is a weekend, and they are making dinner for the whole family.
items.vi: Mô tả ảnh bằng thì hiện tại tiếp diễn (are cooking), nói người trong ảnh và cảm xúc của họ (I think they are happy).

parts.instr: Talk about the task with your partner.
parts.instrVi: Thảo luận nhiệm vụ.

items.q: Your school wants to plan a sports day for all students. Talk about which activities could be included and choose the best two.
items.sample: I think a sports day could include running races, a football match, a relay and a tug of war. Running races are good because everyone can join in, even students who do not play sports. A tug of war is fun as a team game, and it is easy to organize. In my opinion, the best two are the relay and the tug of war, because both are team events and they make students laugh and cheer for each other.
items.vi: Đưa ra nhiều ý tưởng rồi chọn hai hoạt động tốt nhất và giải thích bằng because; dùng I think, In my opinion.

parts.instr: Give your opinion.
parts.instrVi: Nêu ý kiến của bạn.

items.q: Do you think sports competitions at school are a good idea? Why or why not?
items.sample: I think sports competitions at school are a good idea, because they teach students to work as a team and they keep us healthy. However, some students feel nervous when they lose, so teachers should give small prizes to everyone who takes part. In my school we have a race every year, and I always look forward to it.
items.vi: Nêu ý kiến rõ ràng (I think), đưa lý do (because) và một ý đối lập (however).

parts.instrVi: Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn bức tranh đúng.

audio.t: What did Lucy buy at the market?
Did you find a present for your sister, Lucy?
I looked at the scarves and the hats, but she has plenty of those. In the end I bought her a leather bag.

Are you still saving for the game console, Ben?

Is the sale on jackets?
No, jackets and socks are still full price this week. Only the jeans are reduced.

audio.t: Where did the girl find her purse?
Did you find your purse?
Yes! I thought I left it on the bus or at school, but the supermarket manager phoned me. It was under the shelf near the milk.

items.vi: Quản lý siêu thị gọi điện: ví nằm dưới kệ gần sữa, không phải trên xe buýt hay ở trường.

audio.t: What did the man buy for his father?

items.vi: Bố đã có quá nhiều đồng hồ và hay đọc sách, nên anh mua tai nghe để nghe nhạc.

audio.t: What sold out first at the school sale?
How was the school sale?
Great. Cookies and books were still on the table at the end, but all the cakes were gone by ten o'clock.

parts.instrVi: Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn đáp án đúng.

I bought these shoes online and they came in two days.
I never do that. I like to try things on, and sending them back is such a bother.

Fair point. Let us try monthly payments for three months.

I love the color, but it costs more than I planned, so I will wait for the sale.

It is too big for her.
She does not like the color.

I bought these headphones last week and one side has already stopped working. At least I kept the receipt, so the shop will give me a new pair.

audio.t: Why does the man walk to school?
Why are you walking? Where is your bike?
The bike is fine. I am saving money. The bus costs three dollars each way, and walking is free and good exercise.

items.q: Why does the man walk to school?
items.vi: Xe đạp không hỏng; anh đi bộ để tiết kiệm tiền vé xe buýt.

parts.instr: You will hear a radio presenter talking about a market. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.instrVi: Bạn sẽ nghe một người dẫn radio nói về một khu chợ. Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn đáp án đúng.

audio.t: Hello and welcome to Teen Money Hour. Today I am talking about the Saturday Swap Market in Riverside Hall, which has become very popular with young people in our town.
The market started two years ago, when a group of students wanted to find a cheaper way to buy clothes. At first there were only ten stalls, but now there are nearly fifty.

You can buy jackets, jeans and shoes for about a quarter of the shop price. Everything is second-hand, but it must be clean and in good condition. If you do not want to spend any money, you can also swap: bring two items and take one home.

The market is open every Saturday from nine until two, and the entrance is on Bridge Street. Parking is difficult, so I suggest you come by bike or bus. Entry is free, and visitors who bring their own bag get a free drink at the cafe.
Last week I spoke to the organizer, Mr. Hart. He said the best items are usually sold early, before ten, but prices go down in the afternoon, so if you like to bargain, come after one o'clock.
The money from the stalls pays for the hall, and anything left goes to the town youth center, which will buy new sports equipment this year. So next Saturday, why not go and see for yourself?

items.q: Why did the students start the market?
options: To find a cheaper way to buy clothes
items.vi: Nhóm sinh viên muốn tìm cách mua quần áo rẻ hơn.

items.q: How many stalls are there now?
items.vi: Ban đầu chỉ có mười quầy, nay gần năm mươi.

items.q: What can visitors do if they do not want to spend money?
options: Ask for free items at the cafe
Bring two items and take one home
items.vi: Có thể đổi đồ: mang hai món và mang về một món.

items.vi: Khách mang túi riêng được tặng một đồ uống miễn phí.

items.q: When are the best items usually sold?
items.vi: Món tốt nhất thường bán hết trước mười giờ; giá giảm vào buổi chiều.

items.q: What will the youth center buy this year?
items.vi: Tiền còn lại dùng để mua dụng cụ thể thao cho trung tâm thanh niên.

parts.instr: You will hear an interview with a teenager who runs an online shop. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.instrVi: Bạn sẽ nghe phỏng vấn một thiếu niên điều hành cửa hàng trực tuyến. Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn đáp án đúng.

audio.t: Today my guest is Ben Carter, who is sixteen and runs a small online shop selling handmade leather bracelets. Ben, how did it start?

It was an accident, really. I made a bracelet for my brother's birthday, and his friends asked where he got it. They wanted to buy one, so I made five more and sold them at school for four dollars each.
And then you went online?
Yes, my sister helped me set up a shop page. The first month I sold only three, which was disappointing, but then a local blogger wrote about my bracelets and I sold sixty in a week.
Sixty! How do you manage with school?
I make them on Sunday afternoons, about twenty at a time. During exams I close the shop for two weeks, because my parents said school comes first.
What do you do with the money?
Half goes into my savings account. I also bought a better tool for cutting leather. And a little goes to my grandmother's garden club, because she lent me the money for my first materials.
What is the hardest part?
Honestly, the prices. If I charge too much, nobody buys, but if I charge too little, I earn nothing. I am still learning.
Any advice for other teenagers?
Start small, do not borrow much money, and do not give up after a slow month.

options: His brother's friends wanted to buy them

parts.instrVi: Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn đáp án đúng.

items.text: Customers: Please keep your receipt. We can only change or refund items within fourteen days, and only with proof of purchase.

items.text: Piggy Bank Club, Saturday 10 a.m. Learn how to save and plan. Every child who opens a savings account this month gets a free notebook and pen. Parents are welcome.
items.q: Who gets a free gift?

Willow Market
An open-air food market every Thursday and Saturday, from seven in the morning until five. Local farmers sell fresh fruit, vegetables and cheese. Most stalls take cash only. After three o'clock many sellers lower their prices, so it is a good time to bargain.

Tech Corner

items.text:
My No-Spend Challenge

Last January, I made a decision that surprised my friends and my family: for three months I would not buy anything I did not need. It started after I looked at my bank statement and realized that I had spent most of my birthday money on snacks, phone covers and clothes that I hardly ever wore.

The rules were simple. I could pay for food, school things and bus tickets, but nothing else. No new clothes, no games and no cafe drinks. At first, I thought it would be easy. By the second week, however, I was bored and a little annoyed, especially on Saturdays, when my friends went to the mall and I stayed at home.

Things slowly changed. Instead of shopping, I started to borrow books from the library and to cook with my grandmother, who taught me to make soup and bread. I also discovered that I could swap clothes with my cousin. She gave me a jacket I loved, and I gave her two scarves. Neither of us paid a cent.

The biggest surprise was how I felt about money. When I used to buy something, I felt happy for about an hour and then forgot about it. After the challenge, I thought carefully before every purchase and asked myself one question: "Will I still want this in a month?" Most of the time, the answer was no.

By the end of March, I had saved one hundred and twenty dollars. I did not spend it all at once. I bought a good pair of running shoes, which I really needed, and put the rest in my savings account. I am not saying that shopping is bad, and I still enjoy a trip to the mall with friends. But now I go with a list and a limit.

Some people think that saving money means being unhappy, but I disagree. My challenge showed me that I can have a good time without spending much, and that I control my money, not the other way round. If you are thinking of trying something similar, my advice is to start with one month and tell your friends, so they can support you.

items.q:
Read the email from your English friend Sam and write a reply of about 100 words.

Hi! My cousin's birthday is next week and I only have twenty dollars to spend on a present. I do not know what to buy. Do you have any ideas? Also, do you spend your pocket money quickly or save it? I would love to hear about the best thing you ever bought.

Write about: ideas for a cheap present, how you use your pocket money, and the best thing you ever bought.
items.sample: Hi Sam, thanks for your email. Twenty dollars is a good budget for a present! I think you could buy a nice book or a small plant, because many people love them and they are not expensive. You could also make a card yourself, which makes the present more personal. About my pocket money, I usually save half of it and spend the rest on snacks and small things. Last year I saved for three months and bought a pair of good headphones. They are the best thing I ever bought, because I use them every day for music and online lessons. Tell me what you decide, and good luck!
items.vi: Trả lời đủ ba ý: gợi ý quà rẻ, cách dùng tiền tiêu vặt, món đồ tốt nhất từng mua; dùng văn phong thân mật.

items.q:
You see this announcement in an English-language magazine for teenagers.

Articles wanted: Is it better to save money or to spend it?
Tell us what you think and give reasons. The best articles will be published next month.

Write your article (about 100 words).
items.sample: Is it better to save money or to spend it? In my opinion, we should do both, but saving is a little more important. First, when you save money, you can buy something big in the future, such as a bike or a trip with friends. Second, having some savings makes you feel safe if something unexpected happens. However, I do not think that teenagers should never spend. Spending a small amount on a cinema ticket or a snack with friends makes life more fun. My advice is simple: put aside a part of your money every week, and use the rest carefully. This way you enjoy today and prepare for tomorrow.

audio.t: Hello, everyone, and welcome to the open day at Riverside Swimming Club. My name is Hana Kerr, and I have been the head coach here for eight years. The club itself is older than that. It opened thirty years ago, when it had only one small pool.

We now have two pools, and training is in three groups. Beginners swim on Tuesday evenings. The improvers group meets on Thursdays at five o'clock, and the competition group trains every morning before school, at six thirty. Do not worry, nobody has to join the morning group unless they really want to.
Membership costs thirty dollars a month. If two children from the same family join, the second one pays half. That is much cheaper than the club in the next town, which charges fifty dollars.

Please bring a towel, a swimming cap and goggles. We have lockers, but you need to bring your own lock. You do not need to buy a swimsuit from our shop, though many members like our blue ones. Please shower before you enter the pool.

Every spring we organize a friendly competition with three other clubs. It is not only for fast swimmers. There are races for beginners, and there is a relay where parents can take part too. Last year the youngest swimmer was seven years old.

If you want to join, you can write to us through our website or fill in a form at the desk today. Please do not telephone before six p.m., because the office is closed. Now, let's take a tour of the pool.

audio.t: My guest today is Eli Torres, who became the junior chess champion of his region last month at the age of fifteen. Eli, congratulations. When did you learn to play?
My grandfather taught me when I was six. He played with me every Sunday afternoon, and he always let me win at the start. I only understood that later.
How much do you practice now?
About two hours a day, but not all of it is playing. I study old games and try to find the mistakes. Some people think this is boring, but I find it as exciting as a detective story.
Was the final difficult?

The final itself was fine. The hardest game was the semi-final, because my opponent was much older, and I lost an important piece very early. I nearly gave up, but I remembered what my grandfather always said: a game is never finished until the king falls.
Do you get nervous?
Always before a game, never during it. When I start thinking about the board, I forget everything else. My coach teaches me to take three deep breaths at the beginning.
Many people say chess is only for clever people. Do you agree?
Not at all. It is about patience more than intelligence. I am not the best student at school, but I can sit and think for a long time.
What are your plans?

In July there is a national tournament in the capital. I would love to win, but my main goal is to enjoy it. After that I want to start a chess club at my school, because only five students play at the moment.

items.text:
Three summer language courses

A. Lakeside Language Camp
A two-week camp for students aged 11 to 15. Everything is in English, even at meals, and there is a rule that nobody may speak their own language. In the afternoons there are sports, games and a talent show, and students sleep in cabins with new friends. The price is $900, with all food included.

B. City Talk Academy
Evening classes for Korean, German or Chinese, held on Mondays and Wednesdays from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m. for six weeks. The groups are small, with a maximum of eight students, and everyone receives an official certificate that shows their level at the end. The course costs only $240.

C. Home Stay Spanish
Three weeks in a small town in Spain for students aged 15 and over. Each student lives with a local family and has their own room. There are classes every morning, and the afternoons are free for visits and activities with the host family. The price is $1,500, including the flight.

items.text:
My grandmother Lucia lives in a village in Portugal, and until last year I could not have a real conversation with her. She speaks no English, and my Portuguese was limited to hello, thank you and the names of a few foods. Every phone call ended with my mother translating, and I hated feeling like a stranger in my own family.

So last January I decided to learn the language properly. My first plan was simple: a grammar book and half an hour of study every evening. After three weeks I knew a hundred words, but I could not understand a single sentence in a film. I felt discouraged and nearly stopped.

Then my teacher, Mr. Silva, gave me some advice that changed everything. He told me that nobody learns a language by only reading about it; you have to use it, even badly. So I started to leave notes in Portuguese around the house, and I sang along to songs with the words on my phone. I also found an online partner, a boy from Lisbon who wanted to improve his English. Twice a week we talked for twenty minutes, ten in each language. At first we both made terrible mistakes and laughed a lot, which made it easier to continue. Once I confused two words and told him that I had eaten my cousin for lunch instead of a sandwich. He laughed so much that he could not speak for a minute, and I never forgot the right word again.

In August I flew to Portugal. On the first evening my grandmother and I sat in her kitchen, and I managed to talk for almost an hour. I did not understand everything, and she smiled at my accent, but she held my hand and told me she was proud of me. That was worth more than any exam result. I still study every day, and next year I would like to start Italian, because the two languages are similar. But first I want to learn my grandmother's recipes.

options: She wanted to work in Portugal.
She needed a better mark at school.
She wanted to talk to her grandmother without help.

items.q:
Read the email from your English friend Alex and write a reply of about 100 words.

Hi! It is my dad's fortieth birthday next month, and I want to cook a surprise dinner for him at home. I am not a very good cook, so I need ideas. What do you think I should make? Could you help me on the day? Also, tell me about the best surprise you have ever had.

Write about: what Alex should cook, whether you can help on the day, and the best surprise you have ever had.
items.sample: Hi Alex, thanks for your email. What a lovely idea to cook a surprise dinner for your dad! I think you should make something simple, like roast chicken with potatoes and a big salad. For dessert you could bake a chocolate cake, because it is easy and everybody likes it. I would love to help you on the day. I can come two hours early to cut the vegetables and decorate the table. Just tell me the time and the address. The best surprise I have ever had was last year, when my cousins visited me on my birthday. I did not know they were coming, and I was so happy that I almost cried. I hope your dad enjoys the dinner. Write soon! Best wishes, Minh
items.vi: Trả lời đủ ba ý: gợi ý món nấu, có giúp được vào ngày đó không, và kể về một bất ngờ tuyệt nhất của bạn. Dùng giọng thân mật.

items.q: Your English teacher has asked you to write an article for the school magazine. The title of the article is: A game or sport that everyone should try. Write your article in about 100 words.
items.sample: A game or sport that everyone should try is table tennis. First of all, it is cheap, because you only need a table, a small ball and two bats. Many schools and clubs have tables that students can use for free. Second, it is fun for everybody. You can play it with friends or with your family, and the rules are easy to learn. Playing also helps you to react quickly and to concentrate. Finally, it is a great way to make new friends. At my school, a group of students plays together every lunchtime, and anybody can join them. If you have never played before, I really think you should try it. You will probably love it.

audio.t: Hello, listeners. This week I am visiting Hillside Cheese Farm, which is open to visitors all year round.
There are two tours every day, one at ten in the morning and one at two in the afternoon. The tour costs eight dollars, but children under twelve do not pay anything.

At eleven o'clock you can watch the cows being milked, and afterwards you can taste five different kinds of cheese. The most unusual one is the goat cheese. The goats eat wild mountain herbs, and that gives the cheese a sweet, flowery flavor.
One piece of advice. Bring a warm jacket, because the cheese cellar is very cold, even in summer. And if you come by car, please leave it behind the big red barn, not in front of the shop.
The farm shop sells cheese, butter and homemade bread, and there is a small cafe where you can have lunch. It really is a lovely day out for all the family.

audio.t: Today I am talking to Mira Vale, who won the national junior chess title last month. Mira, how did you start?
My grandfather taught me when I was six. I thought it was just a game for old people, but I soon loved it.
How much do you practice?
About an hour every evening, and longer at weekends. Some people think that is too much, but it never feels like work to me.
What is the hardest part of playing chess?
Staying calm when I am losing. The moves are not the problem. Sometimes I get angry with myself, and then I make more mistakes.
What do you do before an important game?
I go for a short walk and leave my phone in my bag. Some players listen to music, but I prefer silence.
And what are your plans for the future?
I would like to study math at university, and one day I want to coach young children. Being a professional player is not my main dream.
What advice would you give to beginners?
Play against people who are better than you. You will lose a lot at first, but that is how you learn.

items.text:
Three sea holidays for young people

A. Sailing Week, Port Lenno
Five days on a small sailing boat with an instructor. You learn to steer and read the wind. No experience is needed, but you must be able to swim. Ages 13 to 16. Price: $320, including all meals. Groups of six.

B. Reef Explorers, Palm Cove
A week of snorkeling and diving classes in warm, clear water. Each day starts with a lesson about fish and coral. You sleep in a hostel on the beach. Beginners are welcome from age 12, and equipment is provided. Price: $450, meals not included.

C. Whale Watch Camp, Northern Point
Three days on the cold northern coast, watching whales from a boat and from the cliffs. Evenings are spent in a cabin with a scientist who explains how whales communicate. You do not need to swim, and the trip is suitable for families. Price: $210, with warm clothes lent to guests.

items.text:
The Night the Turtles Come

Every year between June and September, hundreds of sea turtles climb onto the beaches of Coral Bay to lay their eggs. For the people of the village, this is the most important time of the year, and for me it was a dream come true when my uncle, a turtle guide, invited me to join him for a week.

On the first evening, I was surprised by the rules. We could not use flashlights, because bright light confuses the turtles and sends them back to the sea. We wore dark clothes, spoke in whispers and stayed far from the nests. At first I thought this was a little too strict, but after I watched a huge female turtle slowly dig a hole in the sand, I understood. She was nervous, and the smallest noise could have stopped her.

My uncle explained that only one baby turtle in a thousand survives to become an adult. Birds, crabs and big fish eat the babies, and plastic bags in the water are another danger, because turtles think they are jellyfish. That is why the village now has a plastic-free beach, and the local school teaches every child to protect the nests.

The best moment came on the fifth night. Around midnight, about eighty baby turtles pushed their way out of the sand at the same time and rushed toward the waves, no bigger than my hand. I wanted to help them, but my uncle gently stopped me. "They must make the journey alone," he said. "Walking to the sea is how they learn where home is, and it is how they will find this beach again in twenty years."

Before I left, I joined the village team that counts the nests each morning. The numbers are rising slowly, which gives people hope. I came to Coral Bay as a visitor, but I left feeling that I had learned something much bigger than a list of facts. If we want wild animals to survive, we sometimes need to do less, not more.

items.q:
Read the email from your English friend Sam and write a reply of about 100 words.

Hi! My school is holding a baking contest next month and I want to enter. I cannot decide what to bake. Which cake or cookies would you choose? Have you ever cooked for a lot of people? Could you come to my house on Saturday to practice with me?

Write about: what Sam should bake, a time you cooked for many people, and whether you can come on Saturday.
items.sample: Hi Sam, thanks for your email. A baking contest sounds like great fun! I think you should bake chocolate cookies, because they are easy to make and everybody loves them. You could also add some nuts on top to make them look special. Last year I cooked a big pot of vegetable soup for twenty people at my grandmother's birthday party. I was very nervous, but everyone enjoyed it, and I felt proud. I would love to come to your house on Saturday to practice with you. I am free all afternoon, so I can arrive at two o'clock. Shall I bring some eggs and sugar? See you soon! Best wishes, Tam

items.q:
Your English teacher has asked you to write a story. Your story must begin with this sentence: The mountain path was covered in fog when we started to climb.

Write your story in about 100 words.
items.sample: The mountain path was covered in fog when we started to climb. My brother and I were walking to a small cabin where our grandfather was waiting for us. After an hour the fog became so thick that we could not see the path, and my brother's face looked worried. I stayed calm and remembered my father's advice: never leave the path and wait for help. We sat on a rock and I blew my whistle three times. Soon we heard a dog barking, and a friendly farmer appeared with a flashlight. He took us to the cabin, where our grandfather was cooking hot soup. It was the scariest and the best climb of my life.

Football is fun, but it needs a big field and many players. Tug of war is good for working together, but it can be tiring. So in my opinion the best two activities are the relay and tug of war, because they bring the whole class together.

audio.t: Hello, everyone, and thank you for coming to the open evening for the Pinewood Hiking Club. I am Dana Whitfield, and I have led the club for six years.
We meet on the second Saturday of every month. Some people think we start at dawn, but we actually leave the school car park at nine, so nobody has to get up too early.
Our walks are usually between eight and twelve kilometers. Last year we tried a twenty-kilometer route, but it was too long for the younger members, so this year the longest walk is fifteen.
You do not need expensive equipment. What matters most is a good pair of boots. Many beginners buy a big backpack first, but you only need a small one for water and lunch.

Safety is very important. Every group has two adult leaders, and we always check the weather forecast the night before. If there is a storm warning, we cancel the walk and tell everyone by text message.
Members also learn useful skills, like reading a map. Last spring, a group of beginners found their way back to the bus using only a map and a compass, which was a proud moment for them.

Joining costs thirty dollars for the year. That covers transport, a club T-shirt and a small first aid kit. If you would like to join, take a form from the table by the door and bring it back next week with a parent's signature.

audio.t: Today I am talking to seventeen-year-old Maya Torres, who runs her own bread stall at the Saturday market. Maya, how did it all start?
My grandmother taught me. I used to watch her bake when I was seven, but I only started selling bread when a neighbor tasted my loaves and asked if she could buy some.
Was it difficult to run a stall?
The hard part was the early mornings. I get up at four on Saturdays to bake. I never expected to enjoy that, but now I love the quiet kitchen.
What do you spend the money on?
Some goes on flour and other ingredients, of course. I am saving the rest for a baking course in the summer. I would like a better oven too, but that has to wait.
How do you manage school and the business?
It is tough in exam season. My parents help by delivering orders, and I make a weekly plan. If I have a big test, I skip the market that week.
What is the best part of the job?
Honestly, seeing regular customers come back. One old man buys a seeded loaf every week and tells me about the bread his mother used to make. That means more to me than the money.
Any advice for teenagers who want to start something similar?
Start small. I began with just six loaves, and I only added more when I knew I could sell them. And do not worry if your first attempts fail. Mine were as hard as rocks!

items.text:
Three museums to visit this summer
A. The Old Mill Museum
This small museum is in a restored flour mill beside the River Aldin. Visitors can watch the machinery work and, on Sundays, help to grind real wheat. It is a good place for families because there are special activity sheets for children, and the cafe sells bread baked with the mill's own flour. There is no guided tour, but staff are happy to answer questions. Open every day except Monday.
B. The Harbor Maritime Museum
Housed in a former customs building, this museum tells the story of the port from the 1600s to today. There are model ships, old maps and a collection of sailors' letters. Each evening at six, a guide leads a free tour in English, French or Spanish. The museum has an elevator, so wheelchair users can reach every floor. Tickets must be bought online in advance.
C. The Stonegate Castle Museum
High on a hill above the town, this museum is inside a thirteenth-century castle. You can walk along the walls and try on copies of medieval clothes. The path up the hill is steep, and there is no elevator, but a small bus runs from the town square every hour. Visitors with a student card get half-price tickets. Photography is not allowed inside the towers.

items.text:
When I started working as a museum guide in the small town of Wexbury, I believed that the most important rule was simple: never touch anything. Glass cases, ropes and warning signs were everywhere, and my job was to keep visitors at a safe distance from the objects. Then, one rainy afternoon, a group of ten-year-olds changed my mind.

The children were visiting our exhibition on life in the Iron Age. They had listened politely while I talked about pots and tools, but I could see their attention drifting. Finally, a girl put up her hand and asked, "Can we hold something that old?" I said no, as usual. She looked so disappointed that I went to the storeroom and brought out a copy of an Iron Age cup, made by a local potter. The mood in the room changed at once. The children passed the cup around, asking how it was made, who drank from it and why the handle was so small. They remembered more from those ten minutes than from the whole hour before.

Since then, our museum has introduced a "handling table" where visitors can touch carefully chosen objects. Not everyone agrees with the idea. Some colleagues argue that even copies encourage people to forget that real objects are fragile. I understand these worries, so we have made rules: only clean hands, only one object at a time, and always with a guide nearby.

However, the results speak for themselves. The number of school visits has doubled in two years, and teachers tell us that pupils talk about the exhibition for weeks afterwards. Last month, an older man who had not been to a museum since he was a boy spent almost an hour at the table, telling his grandson how his own father used to make similar tools.

Of course, nothing can replace the feeling of standing in front of a genuine object that is two thousand years old. That is why the real cup still sits behind glass in the main hall. But I now believe that a museum should do more than protect the past. It should help people feel close to it, and sometimes that means letting them pick it up.

audio.t: Welcome to Weekend Matters. Today I'm talking about the Young Cooks Club, which opens next month at the community center in Greenfield. The club was started by a retired chef called Mr. Okafor, who noticed that many teenagers in the area ate fast food every day because they had never learned to cook. He began with just four students in his own kitchen. Now the club has a big room with twelve cookers, and it meets every Wednesday after school. New members must be between twelve and sixteen. There is no fee, but each student brings a small bag of ingredients, which they share. In the first month, students learn basic skills like cutting vegetables safely and making simple sauces. Later, they plan a menu in small teams. The highlight of the year is a dinner in June, when members cook for their families. Last year, a girl called Hana made a soup so good that a local restaurant asked for the recipe. Mr. Okafor says the most important lesson isn't about food at all. It's about patience and working together. If you want to join, call the center before the twentieth of this month, because there are only twenty places.

audio.t: Today my guest is Leo Marsh, who is sixteen and plays the drums in a band called Blue Lanterns. Leo, when did you start?
I was nine. My uncle had an old drum kit in his garage, and I just hit everything. My mom says it was the loudest summer of her life.
Did you have lessons?
Yes, but only for a year. My teacher moved away, so after that I learned from videos online. Honestly, I think that made me more creative, because I had to find my own style.
How did the band begin?
Three of us from school entered a talent show. We weren't planning to win, we just wanted to try it. We came second, and a lot of people asked us to play at birthday parties.
Is it difficult to practice and do schoolwork?
It was at first. I used to practice every evening and my grades dropped. Now I practice for an hour after dinner, and only on days when I have no big tests. It works better.
What's the best part of being in a band?
Definitely the moment on stage when everyone is playing together. People think it's the applause, but for me it's the feeling that the whole group is one machine.
And what's next?
We're recording our first songs next month. It's scary, because mistakes can't be hidden in a recording. But I'm really looking forward to it.

parts.instr: Read the article about driverless trains. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.instrVi: Đọc bài báo về tàu không người lái. Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn đáp án đúng.

items.text:
When Marta Silva first heard that her city's new metro line would have no driver, she felt uneasy. "I imagined an empty cabin rushing through a dark tunnel," she says. "It sounded more like a science-fiction film than a way to get to work." Two years later, she rides the line every morning and has changed her mind completely.

Driverless trains are not as new as many people think. Some airport shuttles have run without drivers for decades, and several large cities now operate entire metro lines this way. The trains are controlled by a computer system that receives information from sensors along the track. These sensors tell the system exactly where every train is, so it can keep a safe distance between them. Engineers say this allows trains to arrive more often, sometimes every ninety seconds, which means shorter waits for passengers.

Not everyone is convinced, however. Some travelers worry about what would happen if the system broke down, while others miss having a person at the front who can make announcements. To answer these concerns, most driverless lines still employ staff who walk through the trains, help passengers and deal with emergencies. "We haven't removed people," explains one manager. "We have moved them to where they are most useful."

There are also surprising benefits. Because a computer drives more smoothly than a human, the trains use less electricity and the ride feels gentler. Wheels and brakes wear out more slowly, so repairs cost less. And since nobody has to sit in a small cabin for eight hours, the company can offer its workers more varied jobs.

Looking ahead, researchers are testing ideas that go further still. One project uses small automatic pods that travel on demand, rather than following a timetable. Passengers would book a pod with their phones and travel directly to their destination without stopping at other stations. Experts believe that such a system could one day reduce traffic in crowded city centers. "The technology already exists," says one engineer. "The real challenge is persuading people to trust it."

As for Marta, she now enjoys sitting at the very front window, watching the tunnel lights rush past. "It feels like the future," she laughs, "and it has never once been late."

items.sample: Sara looked at the strange key in her hand and smiled. She had found it under an old tree in her grandmother's garden, and she was sure it opened something special. All afternoon she tried it on every door in the house, but nothing worked. She felt a little sad because she wanted an adventure. Then she remembered the dusty wooden box in the attic. She ran upstairs and moved some old blankets. The box was still there, with a small silver lock. Her hands were shaking when she pushed the key inside. Finally, the lock clicked. Inside the box there were photographs, a map and a letter from her grandmother, written when she was a girl. Sara read it twice and smiled again. It was the best surprise of her summer.

audio.t: Today I am talking to Mira Costa, who is sixteen and has just won a national climbing prize. Mira, welcome. How did you start?
By accident. My cousin took me to an indoor wall for his birthday party when I was nine. I was only going to watch, but the instructor asked me to try, and I loved it.
Was it difficult at first?
Not the climbing itself. My arms were weak, but I was light and learned quickly. What I found hard was my fear of heights, so I started on low walls and moved up slowly.
How often do you train?
Four days a week, two hours each time. Some people think I should train every day, but my coach says rest is as important as practice, and I agree.
Does it affect your schoolwork?
A little. I am tired after training, so I do my homework in the morning before school. My teachers are very helpful.
What advice would you give to beginners?
Do not compare yourself with others. The best climbers are not always the strongest. They are the ones who plan their moves carefully.
And what is next for you?
I hope to go to a climbing camp in the mountains next summer, and I want to try real rock outdoors for the first time.

items.text:
Three school media clubs

Beacon Newsletter
This is the oldest club in the school. Members write articles for a printed paper that comes out every month. You can write about sports, school events or local news, and each writer works with an older student who checks the text before it is printed. The club meets on Mondays. No special equipment is needed. The best article of the year wins a prize at the summer assembly.

Studio Five
This club makes short videos about school life, from interviews with teachers to funny sketches. Members learn how to use cameras and editing software, and the club has enough equipment for everyone to borrow at home. Meetings are on Wednesdays. Some videos are shown on the screen in the entrance hall, and the best ones go on the school website. Members must be at least twelve, and they must ask permission before filming anyone.

Radio Wave
Radio Wave broadcasts a thirty-minute program every Friday lunchtime. Members choose the music, read the news and talk to guests. You do not have to be good with technology, because a teacher controls the sound, but you must feel comfortable speaking in front of others. The club also runs a quiz each term with prizes. New members are welcome at any time, even in the middle of the year.

items.text:
Can you spot the advert?

Last month, I decided to count how many advertisements I saw in one day. I thought it would be easy, but by lunchtime I had lost count. There were posters on the bus, banners on websites, short videos between my favorite songs, and even a famous footballer holding a bottle of water in the background of a friend's photo. Nobody had told me it was an advert, and that was exactly the point.

Advertisers know that teenagers spend a great deal of time online, so they have changed their methods. Instead of a loud television commercial, they often pay popular video makers to mention a product as if it were a casual choice. The video maker smiles, says she loves the new trainers, and her followers believe her. Some of these followers are only ten or eleven years old and cannot tell the difference between honest advice and paid promotion. In many countries, the rules now say that creators must write a clear word such as 'ad' on their posts, but many people forget to read it or never see it.

My teacher, Ms. Ortega, says that advertising is not all bad. A good advert can be creative and funny, and it can tell people about useful new products. She also points out that many free websites and programs only exist because companies pay to be shown there. 'The problem,' she says, 'is not that adverts exist. It is that we stop asking questions about them.'

So I made a list of questions to ask myself whenever I want to buy something. Who made this message? What do they want me to do? Would I still want this thing if no one had shown it to me? The third one is the hardest. I have found that more than half of the things on my wish list disappear when I answer it honestly.

I am not suggesting that we should switch off our phones. That would be impossible and, frankly, a little boring. But I do think we should treat adverts like a magic show: enjoy the performance, but remember that someone is controlling what you see.

To encourage readers to think carefully about adverts

items.q:
Read this email from your English friend Sam and the notes you have made. Write an email to Sam using all your notes. Write 100 words or more.

Hi! Our class is going on a two-day camping trip next month and we can choose one activity. I cannot decide between kayaking, hiking and cooking over a fire. What would you choose? Also, I do not know what to pack. Can you give me some ideas? See you soon, Sam

Notes: choose an activity and give a reason / say what to bring / ask about the tent
items.sample: Hi Sam, Thanks for your email. A camping trip sounds like great fun! I would choose hiking because I love being outside and I like seeing new places. Kayaking is exciting, but I am not a strong swimmer, so I would feel nervous. Cooking over a fire could be fun too, but I think walking in the forest is more relaxing. You should bring a warm jacket, because the nights can be cold, and a good pair of shoes. Do not forget a flashlight, a water bottle and some snacks. I would also bring a small game to play in the evening. Can you tell me who will share a tent with you? Will the teachers give us the tents, or do we need to bring our own? I hope the weather is sunny. Write back soon and tell me what you decide. Best wishes, Kim

items.q: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story. Your story must begin with this sentence: The lights went out just as the show began. Write your story in 100 words or more.
items.sample: The lights went out just as the show began. Everyone in the school hall gasped, and the audience started to talk loudly. I was standing behind the curtain, ready to sing my first song. My hands were shaking and my heart was beating fast. Suddenly, my friend Lena gave me her phone with the flashlight on. She said, Hold it up and sing anyway. I walked onto the stage and began to sing quietly. Slowly, other students took out their phones and lifted them into the air, and the dark hall filled with tiny stars. Nobody talked any more. When the song finished, the lights came back on, and the audience stood up and clapped for a long time. Finally, I understood that the best part of the evening had happened because of the problem. I thanked Lena and smiled all the way home.

items.q: What did you do last weekend?
items.sample: Last weekend I went to my grandmother's house. We cooked lunch together, and then I helped her in the garden.
items.vi: Kể về cuối tuần qua bằng thì quá khứ đơn: went, cooked, helped.

items.q: Do you prefer to spend time with friends or with your family? Why?
items.sample: I prefer to spend time with my family because we can talk about anything, but I also like meeting my friends at the weekend.
items.vi: Chọn một bên bằng prefer và giải thích lý do.

parts.instr: Describe the photo.
parts.instrVi: Mô tả bức ảnh.

items.q: Describe the photo. What are the people doing, and how do they feel?
items.sample: In this photo I can see a family in a living room. They are sitting around a table and playing a board game. The father is holding some cards and he is smiling. The children look very excited, and the girl on the left is laughing. It looks like a comfortable evening at home. I think they are having a great time together, and maybe it is somebody's birthday because there is a cake on the table.
items.vi: Mô tả ai, ở đâu, đang làm gì, cảm xúc thế nào; dùng thì hiện tại tiếp diễn và looks like.

parts.instr: Discuss the ideas and choose the best one.
parts.instrVi: Thảo luận các ý tưởng và chọn ý hay nhất.

items.q: A school wants to organize a day out for students. Here are some ideas: a hiking day, a cooking class, a visit to a farm, a talent show. Talk together about the ideas and decide which one is the best.
items.sample: I think a hiking day is a good idea because students can enjoy fresh air and exercise. A cooking class would be fun too, but not everybody likes cooking. A visit to a farm is interesting for younger students, but older students might find it boring. A talent show is exciting, but only a few students can take part. In my opinion the best choice is the hiking day, because everyone can join and it is cheap.
items.vi: Nêu ưu và nhược điểm của từng ý tưởng rồi chọn một phương án và giải thích.

parts.instr: Answer the opinion question.
parts.instrVi: Trả lời câu hỏi nêu ý kiến.

items.q: Do you think it is better to spend free time outdoors or at home? Why?
items.sample: I think it is better to spend free time outdoors because we get exercise and fresh air, and it is easier to meet friends. However, I also enjoy staying at home sometimes, for example when the weather is bad or when I am tired. At home I can read, listen to music or watch a film. So the best idea is to do both, but I prefer to be outdoors most of the time.
items.vi: Nêu ý kiến rõ ràng, đưa lý do và ví dụ, có thể thừa nhận mặt còn lại.
